Still typing out the same invoice every month? QuickBooks Online can create and email it for you on a schedule.

Here's the 7-step setup, plus the mistakes behind unsent invoices, double-billing and outdated prices 🧵

Start here: Gear icon > Recurring transactions > New > Invoice. Can't find it? Search 'recurring'. It isn't on every plan or user role, so check yours first. Shortcut: open a correct invoice and select Make recurring.

Pick the right template type:
• Scheduled: created and emailed automatically (fixed retainers)
• Reminder: you check it before it's sent
• Unscheduled: saved pre-filled, used on demand
Unsure? Start with Reminder for 1–2 cycles.

Easy-to-miss settings:
• Tick 'send emails automatically' or invoices get created but never sent
• Match the end date or occurrences to the contract (12-month retainer = 12)
• Don't type a month in line descriptions; it repeats every time

Keep it accurate:
• New price in Products and services? Saved templates don't update. Edit each one.
• Pause the old template before making a new one, or the client is billed twice.
• Turn on automatic invoice reminders.

Hourly clients? Skip recurring templates. Bill from billable time entries, and use a recurring template only for a fixed retainer.

Full 7-step guide with menu paths and FAQ (labels vary by version): {URL}

Here's a complete walkthrough for setting up recurring invoices in QuickBooks Online (QBO), plus the mistakes that most often cause problems. Menu labels change between QBO versions, so treat the names below as approximate.

**Before you start**

- Recurring transactions aren't included on every QBO plan or in every region, and some user roles can't use them. Check your subscription settings or Intuit's plan comparison.
- Go to gear icon > Account and settings > Sales. Set your default terms (for example, Net 14), your online payment options and sales tax if you charge it. New templates start from these defaults.

**The setup**

1. **Create the template.** Go to gear icon > Recurring transactions (usually under Lists) > New > Invoice > OK. If you can't see it, type "recurring" into the search bar. Shortcut: open a correct existing invoice for the client and select **Make recurring** at the bottom.
2. **Name it and pick a type.** Use a name you can spot quickly, like "Acme Ltd – Monthly retainer". Then choose a type:
   - **Scheduled:** QBO creates each invoice automatically, and emails it if you turn on auto-send. You can choose how many days in advance it's created.
   - **Reminder:** QBO reminds you to review and create the invoice yourself.
   - **Unscheduled:** a pre-filled invoice with no dates, for use when you need it.
   - If you're unsure, use Reminder for the first one or two cycles.
3. **Set the schedule.** Choose Daily, Weekly, Monthly or Yearly, then the pattern (for example, day 1 of every 1 month, or every 3 months for quarterly billing). The start date is the date of the first invoice. Under End, choose a date or a number of occurrences that matches the contract. A 12-month retainer should end after 12 occurrences.
4. **Add the customer and turn on sending.** Select the customer and check the billing email. Most versions accept several addresses separated by commas. On Scheduled templates, **tick the option to send emails automatically**. Without it, QBO creates the invoices but doesn't send them. Confirm the terms so due dates fill in, and untick Print later if you only send by email.
5. **Add line items.** Write descriptions that stay accurate every cycle, such as "Monthly retainer – services for the billing period". Don't type a month or date, because it will repeat on every invoice. Check the tax setting on each line. If you use QuickBooks Payments, choose which payment methods show on the invoice and check current fees on Intuit's site.
6. **Save and check the first invoice.** Confirm the template shows the right Next date in the Recurring transactions list. When the first invoice is created, open it and check the amount, tax, invoice date, due date and whether it was actually sent.
7. **Turn on reminders.** Go to gear icon > Account and settings > Sales > Reminders and turn on automatic invoice reminders, so overdue invoices get chased for you.

**Common gotchas**

- **Price changes don't carry over.** Changing a price in Products and services doesn't update rates already saved in recurring templates. Edit each affected template yourself.
- **Edits only apply going forward.** Editing a template only changes invoices created after you save it. To fix an invoice that already exists, edit that invoice directly.
- **Watch for double-billing.** Pause or delete the old template *before* you create a replacement, or the client gets billed twice. Pausing keeps the template so you can restart it later. Deleting removes it. Neither one deletes invoices the template already created.
- **Hourly work doesn't fit.** Don't use recurring templates for variable hourly billing. Bill from billable time entries instead. For a fixed retainer plus extra hours, use a recurring template for the retainer and a separate time-based invoice for the hours.
- **Autopay depends on where you are.** In some regions, QuickBooks Payments lets customers set up autopay for recurring invoices. Availability, setup and fees vary by country and plan, so check QuickBooks Help before you offer it to clients.

Happy to answer questions in the comments.

*Disclosure: this is a shortened version of a guide I published on The Wealth Ascent, which also has an FAQ: {URL}. You don't need it to set this up, since everything is covered above.*
